obligation: G091 -- multi-token internal execution, and what it can actually reach

confound_checked_by_building_the_baselin.why: Every amortization_x in NX_MATMUL_K_AMORTIZATION is measured against serial r1k1, which credits the ROW TILING and the MULTI-TOKEN batching together. R tiling needs no multi-token machinery at all -- it is available at K=1 -- so the table could not say how much of r4k4's 2.567x was actually multi-token. Four (R,1) kernels were added to the shader macro and the harness and measured.
confound_checked_by_building_the_baselin.verdict: The confound was real but SMALL. Kernel tiling alone buys 1.119x; the genuine multi-token component is 2.293x. The measurement CONFIRMS the lever rather than deflating it.
confound_checked_by_building_the_baselin.also_found: r16k1 is 0.812x -- a REGRESSION -- and r4k8, r8k4 and r16k4 all fall back from r4k4. The sweet spot is r4k4 and the surface is not monotone in either axis.

ceiling.statement: At PERFECT acceptance the ceiling is 57.4 TPS if the 9.019 ms non-GEMV remainder does not amortize with K, and 93.8 TPS if it fully does. Neither reaches 100 -- the amortized case comes within 6%. Whether that remainder amortizes is UNMEASURED because the runtime has no batched path, and it is the single number that decides between 57 and 94 TPS.

token_unit_is_unchanged: The verify forbids inflating TPS by changing the token unit. Speculative verification does NOT change it: the external tokenizer is untouched and only ACCEPTED tokens are counted, so TPS here means the same thing it means at K=1 and useful text per wall second moves with it. No internal alphabet or macro unit is proposed.
model_correction: A first pass computed the 'amortized' column as NONGEMV*K/kept, which equals the serial case at perfect acceptance and is simply the same number twice. Corrected: a K=4 step costs 33.638 ms of GEMV plus either 36.076 ms (non-GEMV per position) or 9.019 ms (non-GEMV amortized), divided by the accepted count.
